name: ESP32-4832S040 (Cheap Yellow Display, 4.0in, resistive touch)
summary: The big CYD: 320x480 ST7796 on a 4MB no-PSRAM ESP32, with resistive touch, microSD, an RGB LED and a speaker on board.

render.reason: MEASURED BY penguinOS ITSELF, not by a probe, and then measured again against what the RADIO needs. A bare probe reports free=281612; the OS at app_main reports 148188. Sizing the display from the probe figure asked for 281,280 contiguous DMA bytes out of a 110,592-byte largest block and the board booted blind. band_height is 16, not the 40 that first fit, because fitting is not the test - what matters is what is left afterwards. At 40 rows the two strips take 38,400 bytes and boot ends with 7,168 free; esp_http_server starts, but the AP's DHCP server can no longer allocate a reply, so clients associate and are dropped without ever getting an address. The browser then has nowhere to send a request and the failure looks like a dead web server rather than a starved one. At 16 rows the strips take 15,360 and that memory goes back to the radio. The cost is more SPI transactions per frame - 20 bands instead of 8 - which this board can afford far more easily than it can afford a captive portal that never hands out an IP.

display.pixel_format_reason: The ST7796 DOES have a 16-bit SPI pixel mode, which is the one real advantage it has over the ILI9488 it is otherwise pin-compatible with: two bytes per pixel on the wire instead of three. That is a third off every blit before any other tuning.
display.clock_reason: VERIFIED at 40MHz by the panel prober, which drew a readable label, clean colour bars, a smooth grey ramp and an unbroken stripe field. Higher has not been tried; 40 is where this was proven and there is no measurement yet to justify moving it.
display.byte_swap_reason: VERIFIED true, and the instrument was the BACKGROUND, not a primary. cyd-amber declares bg as 38,38,36 - a near-black warm grey - and the panel came up vivid green. Grey is the ideal probe for byte order precisely because it is invariant under a red/blue swap: R, G and B are equal, so channel order cannot move it, and anything that DOES move it must be byte order. The arithmetic is unambiguous - (38,38,36) is 0x2124, and only the byte-swapped reading 0x2421 decodes to a green (32,133,8); every channel-order reading of the unswapped value stays grey. Corroborated by the title bar, which is filled with accent (216,142,86, orange) and rendered blue - the same swapped-byte decode - and which returns to (222,141,82) once the byte order is corrected. NOTE that the prober said the opposite (no-swap + BGR) and was wrong to, exactly as its own caveat warned: it drives this panel through Arduino_GFX, which does its own byte handling, so its colour result never transferred to esp_lcd. color_order stays bgr - with the byte order corrected the observed decode is already RGB-correct, so the two faults were one fault.
display.mirror_reason: VERIFIED true on Y, from the setup screen penguinOS draws itself - the only instrument that works here, for the reason cyd-2432s024n already records: the Arduino prober never calls esp_lcd_panel_mirror, so it cannot test the configuration an OS makes with default arguments. Its passes came out backwards (rot1) or upside down (rot3), 180 apart and neither correctable by rotation. WHAT SETTLED IT was word ORDER, not glyph shape: on the mirrored setup screen the line "scan the code, then open the page" still read left to right in the right sequence, with only the letterforms flipped. A mirror in X reverses the order of the words too; a mirror in Y does not. The two are therefore separable by reading a sentence, with no need to judge which way round a single letter is - which matters, because judging single flipped glyphs is exactly what produced three contradictory readings from the prober.
display.invert_reason: VERIFIED false. Inversion never had to be guessed at here: the three-primary test returned saturated primaries in a recognisable permutation, and an inverting panel would have returned their complements - cyan, yellow, magenta - which is not a result anyone can mistake for red, blue and green.
display.offset_reason: VERIFIED zero. A 240-wide fill reached both edges with no shear and no black column, and the row-count test placed row 0 at the top of the glass.

bluetooth_keyboard.reason: NimBLE is 19KB of heap; Bluedroid is 83KB, which is instant OOM on a board with 20KB free. Release classic-BT memory and bring BLE up BEFORE WiFi, then WiFi.setSleep(true). The K809 keyboard bonds to whichever board it paired with last.

touch.absent_reason: The glass IS resistive touch - the silkscreen says so - but the controller wiring is not established. The CYD family usually puts an XPT2046 on 25/32/39/33/36, and on this board 32 and 25 are ALSO broken out as an I2C header and 35/39 as a spare header, so the community pinout and the silkscreen disagree about who owns those pins. Probe before believing either.

rgb_led.absent_reason: Present on the board, wiring not yet established.

speaker.absent_reason: Present on the board (2-pin header), wiring not yet established.

sdcard.absent_reason: Slot present; the SPI header silkscreen shows the bus at 18/23/19 but the card CS is not confirmed.

bad_baud_rates.reason: arduino-cli's default for this FQBN. Dies immediately after 'Changing baud rate to 921600... Changed.' with 'Unable to verify flash chip connection'. Never wrote a byte.

Inherited from cyd-2432s024n and WRONG here - the two boards have different CH340s. This one starts writing happily and dies mid-image: 57.7% of 907,927 bytes on the measured run, with 'No more data to read from the serial port'. That failure mode is worse than an outright refusal, because it leaves a half-written app partition that will not boot and looks like a bad build.

distinguishing_notes: Do NOT confuse with wavvy-ili9488-40. That entry is a bare 4.0in panel hand-wired to a devkit - no touch, no microSD, no RGB LED, no speaker - and it drives the panel on 18/23/5, which on THIS board is the SPI header and the microSD. Flashing it here drives the SD lines and leaves the glass dark.
Separable from cyd-2432s024n by MAC, and by the glass: 4.0in against 2.4in.
identification.confirm_prompt: Is this the 4.0in board with resistive touch, a microSD slot and a speaker header?

panel_id_register.note: Not attempted. The ILI9488 boards settled that a controller ID read is not something to build on, and this panel was identified the way they were - by drawing a labelled test card under each candidate driver and looking.

gotchas.text: Do NOT reach for wavvy-ili9488-40 because the glass is also 4.0in and also 320x480. That profile is a bare panel hand-wired to a devkit and drives the panel on sck 18 / mosi 23 / cs 5 - which on THIS board is the SPI header and the microSD. Flashing it here drives the card lines and leaves the glass dark. This board is on the CYD set: 14/13/12/2/15 with the backlight on 27.

Settled: this panel needs mirror_y, not mirror_x. Reached by reading WORD ORDER on the setup screen rather than glyph shape - X reverses the order of words, Y does not - after the prober gave three contradictory readings from single flipped letters.

byte_swap is true and was settled on the THEME BACKGROUND, not on a primary: grey is invariant under a red/blue swap, so a grey that turns green indicts byte order and nothing else. The prober had said no-swap and was wrong - it drives the panel through Arduino_GFX, not esp_lcd.

The glass is resistive but the controller wiring is unestablished, and the usual CYD XPT2046 pins (25/32/39/33/36) collide with headers this board brings out for the user: 32 and 25 as I2C, 35 and 39 as spares. Probe before wiring anything to those headers.
